validity.researcher_notes: Read the sheet's own sole cited source (almasryalyoum.com/news/details/3294097, 29-Oct-2024, verified live+content-present) in full. It is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT about this pipeline's identity: the headline and a closing editorial note both call it 'خط منتجات مسطرد- بنها' (Musturad-Banha products line, diameter 16in / length 45km — matching GEM's Diameter/LengthKnown exactly), but the article's own body text describes the actual project as 'مشروع إحلال وتجديد خط المازوت المغذي لشبكة كهرباء مسطرد' (a project to REPLACE/RENEW the mazut line feeding Musturad's power network) whose purpose is 'رفع كفاءة وتأمين نقل المازوت لتغذية محطة كهرباء شبرا الخيمة' (raising efficiency of mazut transport to feed SHUBRA EL-KHEIMA power station) and which 'لم يتم تجديده منذ عام 1984' (has not been renewed since 1984) -- i.e. an aging line feeding a DIFFERENT named destination than Banha. Cross-checked against the Petroleum Pipelines Company's own official FY2023-2024 AGM report, republished near-verbatim by TWO outlets (almasdar.com/146948, verified live; and youm7.com/story/2024/10/10/.../6735756, verified live -- these two are the SAME wire/press-release text, not independent of each other per rule 4). That official company list itemises Egypt's pipeline projects and treats these as TWO SEPARATE, DIFFERENTLY-NAMED items: (1) under 'إحلال وتجديد' (replacement/renewal of existing assets) it lists 'خط مازوت مسطرد / محطة كهرباء شبرا الخيمة' (the Musturad/Shubra El-Kheima mazut line) -- never called 'Banha' anywhere in this text; and (2) under 'رفع الكفاءة' (efficiency-raising/new capacity) it separately lists 'إنشاء خط من مسطرد حتى بنها بطول 52 كم لرفع معدلات تدفيع المنتجات البترولية من منطقة الدلتا إلى مسطرد ومنها إلى السويس' (construction of a NEW 52km Musturad-to-Banha line to boost Delta-to-Suez product throughput) -- this matches P7319 (52km, construction) exactly, both name and length. So the ONLY place in any source that names a 'Musturad-Banha' line at 45km/operating is the one internally-contradictory almasryalyoum article, while the company's own authoritative, twice-published project list names a Musturad-Banha line only at 52km/construction (P7319). Geometry check: fetched both routes from GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes -- P7318.geojson and P7319.geojson are BYTE-IDENTICAL (md5 2def8027a8f54a01e019616f2eeb4e46, same 134 vertices, same start/end coords), and P7319's own RouteNotes already says 'IM: copied the original presumed route but given the increased length it is likely the replacement is taking a different route' -- confirming GEM's own route researcher already recognized P7318 as the 'original' whose route was reused as a stand-in for P7319's 'replacement', i.e. GEM's internal convention already treats these as related-but-distinct (old asset vs. new-build), which is consistent with my reading, not a naive duplicate. Existence/classification are not in doubt (a real petroleum-products/mazut renewal project is genuinely underway per two independently-sourced Oct 2024 news events), and the numeric specs (45km/16in) are exactly as printed in the source -- but they may describe the WRONG-NAMED entity. This is not a duplicate to merge (the two projects appear physically and functionally distinct -- one is a like-for-like renewal of 1980s infrastructure, the other an all-new capacity expansion), but P7318's name/EndLocation rests on a single self-contradictory article and is not corroborated by any other source, so tier is LOW and independent=false pending a resolving source.

summary: concern/attribution: sole source is internally inconsistent (says it feeds Shubra El-Kheima power station, not Banha); PPC's own official project list names the genuine 52km Musturad-Banha new-build as a SEPARATE item matching P7319, whose route geojson is confirmed byte-identical to P7318's (flagged as a copied placeholder in P7319's own RouteNotes).
